Build's clean now — exits 0. What was actually broken (buried under all the deprecation noise, which is harmless):

1. **`src/core/options.js`** — the new bundler passes options as `{ retryCount }`, but this still read `options.retries` (undefined), so `.toFixed(0)` threw. Fixed to read `retryCount`.
2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js`** — the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` instead of `false`, but this had a strict boolean check that threw on anything besides `true`/`false`. Simplified to `flags.backoffEnabled === true`, which treats missing/undefined as disabled (same effective behavior as before, just tolerant of `undefined`).

Both were link-stage failures, not warnings — the build was actually erroring out (`EBUILD02 link-failed`), just scrolled past a screen of deprecation warnings. The remaining 8 warnings in the output are genuine deprecation notices (Node's `Buffer()`, `fs.exists`, punycode, etc.) plus a couple of real-but-non-blocking issues (unused export, circular import) — none of those block the build, so I left them as-is unless you want those addressed too.
